The Mauritian government has today announced that they plan to reform laws on homosexuality. While homosexuality is not explicitly stated as illegal in the law, sodomy is a crime and can lead to upto five years imprisonment. There have been several protests in the past few years opposing this law, mainly by Mauritian LGBT group Collectif Arc en Ciel*. Mauritius will now repeal the illegality of sodomy and continue to work towards equality for its LGBT citizens. Prime Minister Jugnauth has said 'We have today taken the decision to modernise Mauritian law on homosexuality. With this reform we are dedicated to improving the rights of all our citizens. Mauritius is often praised for the integration between many different religions and cultures. We now aim for this to apply to sexual orientation as well'.

With the recent scrutiny over World Cup hosts Russia and their laws on homosexuality, there has also been an increased pressure on many other countries with similar laws. Mauritius and many other African countries have been criticised in the media for such laws. It is believed that part of the reason for this reform is to increase the tourism of those who would otherwise be discouraged by restrictive laws. A Collectif Arc en Cuil representative said 'This is large step towards fighting LGBT inequality in Mauritius. We are pleased this government sees this as a problem. However, there is still much to be done. For example, the recognition of same sex couples'.
